annoying.usageZh: 形容词（Adjective）。描述令人不快或烦躁的人或事。常用结构：find sth/sb annoying；It is annoying when...。口语和书面语都常用，语气比angry轻，侧重“烦人”而非“愤怒”。

examples.sentence: The fly in my room is really annoying.
examples.trans: 我房间里的那只苍蝇真烦人。

examples.sentence: It is annoying when someone talks loudly on the bus.
examples.trans: 有人在公交车上大声说话时，真让人烦。

examples.sentence: My little brother finds it annoying when I borrow his headphones without asking.
examples.trans: 我弟弟觉得我不经允许就借他的耳机很烦人。

examples.sentence: The most annoying part of the job is having to repeat the same instructions every single day.
examples.trans: 这份工作最烦人的地方是每天都要重复同样的指令。

examples.sentence: Rather than confronting his annoying habit of interrupting others, she chose to ignore it politely.
examples.trans: 她没有直接面对他打断别人的烦人习惯，而是选择礼貌地不予理会。

examples.sentence: Persistent notifications from unnecessary apps can be so annoying that users end up deleting them altogether.
examples.trans: 不必要的应用持续推送通知会让人烦到最终干脆把它们全部删掉。

disagreements.usageZh: 名词（Noun），可数，常用复数形式。常用短语：have a disagreement with sb about/over sth；settle/resolve a disagreement。指意见不同或争执，语气比argument温和，可指小分歧也可指原则性分歧。

family.meaning: 令人不愉快的，难相处的

examples.sentence: My sister and I often have small disagreements about TV shows.
examples.trans: 我和妹妹经常因为电视节目有小小的分歧。

examples.sentence: They had a disagreement about whose turn it was to clean the classroom.
examples.trans: 他们因为轮到谁打扫教室而发生了分歧。

examples.sentence: Although they had disagreements on many topics, they still respected each other's opinions.
examples.trans: 虽然他们在很多话题上有分歧，但他们仍然尊重彼此的观点。

examples.sentence: Disagreements between team members are natural, but what matters is how they are resolved.
examples.trans: 团队成员之间有分歧是很自然的，重要的是如何解决这些分歧。

examples.sentence: Unlike personal quarrels, academic disagreements can actually push a field forward when handled constructively.
examples.trans: 与个人争吵不同，学术上的分歧如果得到建设性处理，实际上能推动一个领域向前发展。

examples.sentence: The board meeting dragged on for hours as disagreements over budget allocation revealed deeper conflicts of interest.
examples.trans: 董事会会议拖了好几个小时，因为预算分配上的分歧暴露了更深层的利益冲突。

uncertainty.usageZh: 名词（Noun），不可数，但可加不定冠词表示“一件不确定的事”。常用短语：uncertainty about/over sth；a sense/feeling of uncertainty；economic/political uncertainty。语体偏正式，常见于新闻、学术和书面表达。

examples.sentence: There is some uncertainty about tomorrow's picnic because of the rain.
examples.trans: 因为下雨，明天的野餐有些不确定。

examples.sentence: She felt a lot of uncertainty before the results of the exam came out.
examples.trans: 考试成绩出来之前，她感到非常不确定。

examples.sentence: The uncertainty of the bus schedule made us leave home much earlier than usual.
examples.trans: 公交车时刻表的不确定性让我们比平时早很多出门。

examples.sentence: Facing uncertainty about which major to choose, many students turn to their teachers for guidance.
examples.trans: 面对选哪个专业的不确定性，许多学生向老师寻求指导。

examples.sentence: While uncertainty can be uncomfortable, it often creates space for creativity and new possibilities.
examples.trans: 虽然不确定性可能让人不安，但它往往为创造力和新的可能性留出空间。

examples.sentence: Investors tend to withdraw from emerging markets during periods of heightened political uncertainty, regardless of long-term growth potential.
examples.trans: 在政治不确定性加剧的时期，投资者往往会从新兴市场撤出，而不管其长期增长潜力如何。

admitted.usageZh: 动词 admit 的过去式，意为“承认”。常用结构：admit (that) 从句、admit to doing sth、admit sth。多用于承认错误、事实或内心感受，语气常带不情愿。口语和书面语均常见。

examples.sentence: Tom admitted he ate the last cookie.
examples.trans: 汤姆承认他吃了最后一块饼干。

examples.sentence: She admitted to feeling nervous before the school play.
examples.trans: 她承认在学校话剧演出前感到紧张。

examples.sentence: He admitted that he had copied his friend's homework and said sorry.
examples.trans: 他承认抄了朋友的作业并道了歉。

examples.sentence: Having checked the evidence again, the student admitted making a careless mistake in the experiment.
examples.trans: 再次核对证据后，这名学生承认在实验中犯了一个粗心的错误。

examples.sentence: Although he had denied it for weeks, he finally admitted to hiding the truth from his closest friend.
examples.trans: 尽管他否认了好几个星期，最终还是承认对最亲密的朋友隐瞒了真相。

examples.sentence: Under mounting pressure from the investigation, the official admitted that key safety reports had been deliberately withheld from the public.
examples.trans: 在调查压力不断增大的情况下，这名官员承认关键的安全报告被故意隐瞒，未向公众公开。

doubt.usageZh: 可作动词或名词。作动词时常用 doubt sth / doubt that... / doubt whether...；作名词时常用 have doubts about sth、without doubt、no doubt。表示对事实、能力或可能性感到不确定。口语和书面语均常用。

examples.sentence: I doubt he can come to my birthday party.
examples.trans: 我怀疑他能不能来参加我的生日聚会。

examples.sentence: There is no doubt that our team played better in the second half.
examples.trans: 毫无疑问，我们队在下半场踢得更好。

examples.sentence: She had serious doubts about whether the plan would work in such a short time.
examples.trans: 她严重怀疑这个计划能否在这么短的时间内奏效。

examples.sentence: Given the lack of reliable data, many researchers doubt that the new method is truly more effective.
examples.trans: 由于缺乏可靠数据，许多研究人员怀疑这种新方法是否真的更有效。

examples.sentence: There is little doubt that regular reading broadens one's perspective, yet few teenagers make it a daily habit.
examples.trans: 几乎毫无疑问，经常阅读能拓宽视野，然而很少有青少年把它变成日常习惯。

examples.sentence: While the policy has brought short-term economic gains, experts increasingly doubt whether such benefits can be sustained without serious environmental costs.
examples.trans: 尽管该政策带来了短期经济收益，专家们越来越怀疑这些好处能否在不付出严重环境代价的情况下持续下去。

breakups.usageZh: 名词 breakup 的复数形式，意为“分手；关系破裂”。可指恋爱关系、婚姻、商业合作或团队的解散。常用搭配：go through a breakup、the breakup of a relationship/partnership。口语和书面语均可用。

examples.sentence: My sister was sad after her breakup with her boyfriend.
examples.trans: 我姐姐和男朋友分手后很伤心。

examples.sentence: Breakups are hard, but talking to friends can make you feel better.
examples.trans: 分手很难受，但和朋友聊一聊会让你感觉好一些。

examples.sentence: Many songs are about breakups because almost everyone has experienced that kind of pain.
examples.trans: 很多歌曲都是关于分手的，因为几乎每个人都经历过那种痛苦。

examples.sentence: After several painful breakups, she decided to focus on her studies and personal growth before starting a new relationship.
examples.trans: 经历了几次痛苦的分手后，她决定先专注于学业和个人成长，再开始新的恋情。

examples.sentence: Unlike friendly breakups, those involving betrayal often leave emotional scars that take years to heal.
examples.trans: 与和平分手不同，涉及背叛的分手往往会留下需要多年才能愈合的情感创伤。

examples.sentence: The frequent breakups of coalition governments in the region have made long-term policy planning nearly impossible for successive administrations.
examples.trans: 该地区联合政府的频繁解体使得历届政府几乎无法进行长期政策规划。

complicated.usageZh: 形容词，意为“复杂的，难懂的”。常用于描述问题、情况、机器或说明等。可作定语修饰名词，也可作表语，如“The situation is complicated.”。常见搭配：a complicated problem, get complicated, extremely complicated。

examples.sentence: This math problem is too complicated for me.
examples.trans: 这道数学题对我来说太复杂了。

examples.sentence: The rules of the game are not complicated at all.
examples.trans: 这个游戏的规则一点也不复杂。

examples.sentence: The situation became more complicated after he changed his mind.
examples.trans: 他改变主意后，情况变得更加复杂了。

examples.sentence: Understanding how the human brain works is a complicated task that requires years of study.
examples.trans: 理解人脑如何运作是一项需要多年研究的复杂任务。

examples.sentence: What makes the issue particularly complicated is that both sides have valid arguments.
examples.trans: 让这个问题格外复杂的是，双方都有合理的论点。

examples.sentence: The relationship between economic growth and environmental protection is far more complicated than most policymakers are willing to admit.
examples.trans: 经济增长与环境保护之间的关系远比大多数决策者愿意承认的要复杂得多。

declared.usageZh: 动词 declare 的过去式，意为“宣布，宣告”。常用于正式场合，如政府、组织或个人公开声明某事。常见结构：declare sth, declare that 从句, declare sb/sth + 形容词/名词。语体较正式。

examples.sentence: Our teacher declared the winner of the singing contest.
examples.trans: 我们老师宣布了歌唱比赛的获胜者。

examples.sentence: The company declared that it would stop using plastic bags.
examples.trans: 这家公司宣布将停止使用塑料袋。

examples.sentence: The government declared a state of emergency after the heavy flood.
examples.trans: 洪水过后，政府宣布进入紧急状态。

examples.sentence: Having reviewed all the evidence, the committee declared the results to be valid.
examples.trans: 在审查了所有证据之后，委员会宣布结果有效。

examples.sentence: The country declared its independence in 1947, marking the end of colonial rule.
examples.trans: 该国于1947年宣布独立，标志着殖民统治的结束。

examples.sentence: Despite fierce opposition from several member states, the organization declared the new trade agreement officially in force.
examples.trans: 尽管遭到几个成员国的强烈反对，该组织仍宣布新贸易协定正式生效。

statistics.usageZh: 名词，常用复数形式，意为“统计数字，统计数据”；也可指“统计学”这一学科。常见搭配：according to statistics, official statistics, statistics show/indicate。作主语时谓语动词通常用复数，指学科时用单数。

examples.sentence: The statistics show that most students like playing basketball.
examples.trans: 统计数据显示大多数学生喜欢打篮球。

examples.sentence: According to the statistics, more people are using bikes to go to work.
examples.trans: 根据统计数据，越来越多的人骑自行车上班。

examples.sentence: The statistics from the survey indicate that reading habits have changed a lot among teenagers.
examples.trans: 调查的统计数据表明，青少年的阅读习惯发生了很大变化。

examples.sentence: Official statistics released last month reveal a steady decline in the unemployment rate.
examples.trans: 上个月发布的官方统计数据显示失业率稳步下降。

examples.sentence: While statistics can provide valuable insights, they often fail to capture the human stories behind the numbers.
examples.trans: 虽然统计数据能提供有价值的见解，但它们往往无法捕捉数字背后的人文故事。

examples.sentence: The statistics cited in the report, drawn from a decade of longitudinal research, challenge the long-held assumption that urbanization inevitably reduces social cohesion.
examples.trans: 报告中引用的统计数据来自长达十年的纵向研究，它们挑战了城市化必然削弱社会凝聚力这一长期存在的假设。

stress.usageZh: 名词（Noun），不可数，指精神或情绪上的压力、紧张。常用搭配：under stress（处于压力之下）、reduce/relieve stress（减压）、cope with stress（应对压力）。也可作动词，表示“强调”，如 stress the importance of...。口语和书面语都常用，正式程度中等。

examples.sentence: I have a lot of stress before the exam.
examples.trans: 考试前我压力很大。

examples.sentence: Listening to music helps me reduce stress after school.
examples.trans: 放学后听音乐帮我减轻压力。

examples.sentence: If you are under too much stress, you may find it hard to sleep well.
examples.trans: 如果你压力太大，可能会发现很难睡好。

examples.sentence: Learning to manage stress effectively is a skill that benefits students throughout their lives.
examples.trans: 学会有效管理压力是一项让学生终身受益的技能。

examples.sentence: Rather than ignoring the signs of stress, it is wiser to identify what triggers it and take action early.
examples.trans: 与其忽视压力的信号，不如找出引发压力的原因并尽早采取行动。

examples.sentence: Chronic stress, if left unaddressed, can weaken the immune system and increase the risk of long-term illness.
examples.trans: 长期压力如果不加以处理，会削弱免疫系统并增加患上长期疾病的风险。

physical.usageZh: 形容词（Adjective），表示“身体的”或“物理的、物质的”。常用搭配：physical health（身体健康）、physical exercise（体育锻炼）、physical strength（体力）、physical change（物理变化）。与 mental（心理的）相对，在健康、教育、科学等话题中都很常用。

examples.sentence: Running is good physical exercise.
examples.trans: 跑步是很好的体育锻炼。

examples.sentence: We should take care of our physical health as well as our mental health.
examples.trans: 我们既要照顾心理健康，也要照顾身体健康。

examples.sentence: Doing physical activities every day can make you feel more energetic.
examples.trans: 每天进行体育活动可以让你感觉更有活力。

examples.sentence: The doctor advised him to avoid intense physical activity until his knee had fully recovered.
examples.trans: 医生建议他在膝盖完全恢复之前避免剧烈运动。

examples.sentence: While academic performance matters, physical well-being should never be sacrificed for higher grades.
examples.trans: 虽然学业成绩很重要，但绝不应为了更高的分数而牺牲身体健康。

examples.sentence: A growing body of evidence suggests that regular physical activity can significantly lower the risk of cardiovascular disease.
examples.trans: 越来越多的证据表明，规律的体育活动可以显著降低患心血管疾病的风险。

understanding.usageZh: 名词（Noun），不可数，表示“理解、领会”或“体谅、谅解”。常用搭配：have a good understanding of（对……有很好的理解）、reach an understanding（达成谅解）、show understanding（表示体谅）。也可作形容词，表示“善解人意的”。在人际交往和学术语境中都很常用。

examples.sentence: Thank you for your understanding.
examples.trans: 谢谢你的理解。

examples.sentence: My teacher has a good understanding of our problems.
examples.trans: 我的老师很了解我们的问题。

examples.sentence: A true friend shows understanding when you make a mistake.
examples.trans: 真正的朋友在你犯错时会表示理解。

examples.sentence: Having a deep understanding of cultural differences is essential when working in an international team.
examples.trans: 在国际团队中工作时，深入了解文化差异是必不可少的。

examples.sentence: True understanding goes beyond simply hearing words; it involves recognizing the emotions behind them.
examples.trans: 真正的理解不仅仅是听到话语，还包括识别话语背后的情感。

examples.sentence: A nuanced understanding of historical context is crucial for interpreting the significance of these political reforms.
examples.trans: 对历史背景的细致入微的理解，对于解读这些政治改革的意义至关重要。

therapist.usageZh: 名词（Noun），可数。常用搭配：family therapist（家庭治疗师），physical therapist（物理治疗师），speech therapist（言语治疗师）。指受过专业训练、提供心理或身体康复治疗的人员，语体偏正式。

examples.sentence: My aunt works as a therapist in a children's hospital.
examples.trans: 我姑姑在一家儿童医院做治疗师。

examples.sentence: The therapist taught him some simple exercises to make his back stronger.
examples.trans: 治疗师教了他一些简单的练习来让他的背部更强壮。

examples.sentence: After the accident, a physical therapist helped him learn to walk again.
examples.trans: 事故之后，一位物理治疗师帮助他重新学习走路。

examples.sentence: Having worked as a family therapist for over a decade, she understands how communication patterns shape relationships.
examples.trans: 作为一名从业十多年的家庭治疗师，她深知沟通模式如何塑造人际关系。

examples.sentence: Rather than simply prescribing medication, the therapist encouraged him to identify the underlying causes of his anxiety.
examples.trans: 治疗师没有简单地开药，而是鼓励他找出焦虑背后的深层原因。

examples.sentence: A skilled therapist does not impose solutions but creates a safe space in which clients can arrive at their own insights.
examples.trans: 一位熟练的治疗师不会强加解决方案，而是创造一个安全的空间，让来访者能够得出自己的领悟。

overcome.usageZh: 动词（Verb），不规则变化：overcome - overcame - overcome。常用结构：overcome difficulties/fears/obstacles，be overcome with emotion（情绪激动不能自持）。指成功战胜困难、恐惧或障碍，可用于具体或抽象语境。

examples.sentence: She overcame her fear of dogs after playing with a friendly puppy.
examples.trans: 和一只友好的小狗玩耍后，她克服了对狗的恐惧。

examples.sentence: He worked hard every day and finally overcame his weakness in math.
examples.trans: 他每天努力学习，终于克服了数学上的薄弱之处。

examples.sentence: Although the team faced many difficulties, they overcame them one by one and won the match.
examples.trans: 尽管队伍面临许多困难，他们一个接一个地克服了它们并赢得了比赛。

examples.sentence: To overcome the language barrier, she spent months immersing herself in English-speaking environments.
examples.trans: 为了克服语言障碍，她花了数月时间让自己沉浸在英语环境中。

examples.sentence: What distinguishes successful people is not the absence of obstacles but the determination to overcome them.
examples.trans: 成功者的与众不同之处不在于没有障碍，而在于克服障碍的决心。

examples.sentence: The ability to overcome setbacks without losing sight of one's long-term goals is widely regarded as a defining trait of resilient individuals.
examples.trans: 在不忽视长期目标的前提下克服挫折的能力，被广泛认为是坚韧个体的标志性特质。

jealous.usageZh: 形容词（Adjective）。常用结构：be jealous of sb/sth（嫉妒某人/某物），a jealous husband/wife（爱吃醋的丈夫/妻子）。指因别人拥有自己渴望的东西而感到不满或不安，也可指在感情关系中害怕失去对方的关注。

examples.sentence: My little brother gets jealous when Mom hugs me first.
examples.trans: 妈妈先抱我的时候，我弟弟就会嫉妒。

examples.sentence: She felt jealous when her best friend won the first prize in the speech contest.
examples.trans: 当她最好的朋友在演讲比赛中获得一等奖时，她感到嫉妒。

examples.sentence: He tried not to be jealous of his cousin's new bike, but it was really cool.
examples.trans: 他尽量不去嫉妒表哥的新自行车，但那辆车实在太酷了。

examples.sentence: Instead of feeling jealous of her colleague's promotion, she chose to learn from his work ethic.
examples.trans: 她没有嫉妒同事的升职，而是选择学习他的工作态度。

examples.sentence: Jealous of the attention his sister received, the boy began to act out in ways that alarmed his parents.
examples.trans: 由于嫉妒妹妹得到的关注，这个男孩开始以令父母警觉的方式表现自己。

examples.sentence: While a certain degree of jealousy is natural in competitive environments, allowing it to dictate one's decisions rarely leads to constructive outcomes.
examples.trans: 尽管在竞争环境中一定程度的嫉妒是自然的，但让它左右自己的决定很少能带来建设性的结果。

isolation.usageZh: 名词（Noun），不可数。常用短语：social isolation（社会孤立），self-isolation（自我隔离）。指与他人分开、独自一人的状态，可描述物理上的隔离或心理上的孤立感。

examples.sentence: The sick cat stayed in isolation so other animals would not get ill.
examples.trans: 生病的猫被隔离起来，这样其他动物就不会生病。

examples.sentence: After moving to a new city, she felt a deep sense of isolation until she joined a reading club.
examples.trans: 搬到新城市后，她感到深深的孤立，直到加入了一个读书俱乐部。

examples.sentence: Doctors recommend self-isolation for people who show clear signs of the flu.
examples.trans: 医生建议出现明显流感症状的人进行自我隔离。

examples.sentence: Working from home for months taught him that isolation can quietly affect a person's mood and motivation.
examples.trans: 在家工作几个月让他明白，孤立会悄悄影响一个人的情绪和动力。

examples.sentence: The study highlights a troubling link between prolonged social isolation and declining mental health among elderly residents.
examples.trans: 这项研究突显了老年居民长期社会孤立与心理健康下降之间令人担忧的联系。

examples.sentence: While isolation is sometimes necessary to contain an outbreak, public health officials must also address the psychological toll it takes on communities.
examples.trans: 虽然隔离有时是控制疫情所必需的，但公共卫生官员也必须应对它给社区带来的心理伤害。

communication.usageZh: 名词（Noun），不可数。常用短语：face-to-face communication（面对面交流），effective communication（有效沟通），communication skills（沟通技巧）。指信息、想法或情感的传递过程，可用于日常对话、职场、教育等语境。

examples.sentence: Good communication helps friends understand each other better.
examples.trans: 良好的沟通帮助朋友更好地理解彼此。

examples.sentence: Text messages are fast, but face-to-face communication shows more care and respect.
examples.trans: 短信很快，但面对面的交流更能体现关心和尊重。

examples.sentence: Clear communication between parents and teachers can prevent many small problems from growing bigger.
examples.trans: 家长和老师之间清晰的沟通可以防止许多小问题变大。

examples.sentence: Effective communication involves not only speaking clearly but also listening with full attention.
examples.trans: 有效沟通不仅包括清晰表达，还包括全神贯注地倾听。

examples.sentence: In cross-cultural teams, open communication is often more valuable than technical skill when it comes to building trust.
examples.trans: 在跨文化团队中，建立信任时，开放的沟通往往比技术能力更有价值。

examples.sentence: The rapid evolution of digital communication has reshaped how individuals form relationships, share knowledge, and participate in public life.
examples.trans: 数字通信的快速发展重塑了个人建立关系、分享知识和参与公共生活的方式。

incredibly.usageZh: 副词（Adverb）。用于强调形容词或另一个副词，表示程度极高，相当于“非常、极其”。口语和书面语均可使用，常带有惊讶或赞叹的语气。

examples.sentence: The magician's trick was incredibly cool.
examples.trans: 魔术师的把戏酷极了。

examples.sentence: My grandmother is incredibly good at remembering names and birthdays.
examples.trans: 我奶奶极其擅长记住名字和生日。

examples.sentence: The rescue team worked incredibly fast to reach the trapped hikers before dark.
examples.trans: 救援队行动快得惊人，在天黑前赶到了被困徒步者身边。

examples.sentence: She handled the unexpected questions incredibly calmly, which impressed everyone in the interview room.
examples.trans: 她极其冷静地应对了那些意外问题，给面试室里的每个人都留下了深刻印象。

examples.sentence: The new electric car is incredibly efficient in city traffic, yet it remains remarkably powerful on the highway.
examples.trans: 这款新电动车在城市交通中效率高得惊人，但在高速公路上依然动力强劲。

examples.sentence: Despite facing incredibly harsh conditions, the research team managed to collect enough data to challenge the long-held theory.
examples.trans: 尽管面对极其恶劣的条件，研究团队还是设法收集了足够的数据来挑战那个长期存在的理论。

respectful.usageZh: 形容词，表示“尊敬的，有礼貌的”。常与介词 to 或 towards 搭配，如 be respectful to/towards someone。可用于描述态度、语气、行为等。

examples.sentence: My little brother is always respectful to our grandparents.
examples.trans: 我弟弟总是很尊敬我们的爷爷奶奶。

examples.sentence: We should be respectful when someone is speaking, even if we disagree.
examples.trans: 当别人说话时，即使我们不同意，也应该保持尊重。

examples.sentence: The students remained respectful during the whole ceremony, which made their teacher proud.
examples.trans: 学生们在整个典礼过程中都保持着恭敬的态度，这让他们的老师感到骄傲。

examples.sentence: Being respectful towards people with different opinions is a sign of maturity rather than weakness.
examples.trans: 尊重持不同意见的人是成熟的表现，而不是软弱。

examples.sentence: A respectful tone in professional emails not only reflects good manners but also helps build long-term trust.
examples.trans: 在专业邮件中使用恭敬的语气不仅体现了良好的修养，也有助于建立长期的信任。

examples.sentence: While maintaining a respectful attitude toward tradition, the younger generation is increasingly inclined to question practices that no longer serve the present.
examples.trans: 年轻一代在对传统保持尊重态度的同时，越来越倾向于质疑那些已不再适用于当下的做法。

background.usageZh: 名词，表示“背景”。可指家庭出身、教育经历、文化环境或画面背景。常用搭配：family background（家庭背景）、cultural background（文化背景）、educational background（教育背景）。

examples.sentence: The photo shows a mountain in the background.
examples.trans: 照片的背景是一座山。

examples.sentence: Her family background helped her understand different cultures from an early age.
examples.trans: 她的家庭背景让她从小就能理解不同的文化。

examples.sentence: Students from different backgrounds often bring fresh ideas to group discussions.
examples.trans: 来自不同背景的学生常常能为小组讨论带来新鲜的想法。

examples.sentence: Having a strong background in mathematics gave him a clear advantage when he started learning programming.
examples.trans: 扎实的数学背景让他在开始学习编程时占据了明显的优势。

examples.sentence: The report highlights how a person's socioeconomic background can shape their access to quality education.
examples.trans: 该报告强调了一个人的社会经济背景如何影响其获得优质教育的机会。

examples.sentence: Rather than dismissing her unconventional background, the committee recognized it as a source of insight that conventional candidates rarely possess.
examples.trans: 委员会没有轻视她非传统的背景，反而将其视为一种传统候选人很少具备的洞察力来源。

generation.usageZh: 名词，表示“一代（人）”。指大约同一时期出生或生活的一群人。常用搭配：younger/older generation（年轻/老一代）、future generations（后代）、generation gap（代沟）。

examples.sentence: My grandma tells me stories about her generation.
examples.trans: 我奶奶给我讲她那一代人的故事。

examples.sentence: The older generation often has different ideas about work and life.
examples.trans: 老一代人对工作和生活往往有不同的看法。

examples.sentence: This new generation of smartphones is much faster than the one released two years ago.
examples.trans: 这一代新智能手机比两年前发布的那一代快得多。

examples.sentence: Each generation tends to redefine success according to the economic conditions it grows up in.
examples.trans: 每一代人往往会根据自己成长时期的经济状况来重新定义成功。

examples.sentence: Unlike the previous generation, today's young people are far more likely to prioritize work-life balance over job security.
examples.trans: 与上一代人不同，如今的年轻人更可能优先考虑工作与生活的平衡，而不是工作的稳定性。

examples.sentence: The decisions we make about energy consumption today will determine whether future generations inherit a livable planet or an irreversible crisis.
examples.trans: 我们今天在能源消耗方面所做的决定，将决定后代继承的是一个宜居的星球，还是一场不可逆转的危机。

frighten.usageZh: 动词（Verb）。常用结构：frighten sb（吓到某人）；be frightened of sth（害怕某物）。可作及物动词直接接宾语，也可用于被动语态。口语中常说 You frightened me!（你吓我一跳！）。

examples.sentence: The big dog frightened my little sister.
examples.trans: 那只大狗吓到了我妹妹。

examples.sentence: Don't shout at the baby — you will frighten her.
examples.trans: 别对宝宝大喊大叫，你会吓到她的。

examples.sentence: The sudden noise from the kitchen frightened everyone in the living room.
examples.trans: 厨房里突然传来的响声把客厅里所有人都吓了一跳。

examples.sentence: The idea of speaking in front of hundreds of people frightens me more than anything else.
examples.trans: 在几百人面前演讲这个念头比任何事都更让我害怕。

examples.sentence: What frightened the investors was not the temporary loss, but the company's refusal to explain it.
examples.trans: 让投资者感到恐慌的不是暂时的亏损，而是公司拒绝对此作出解释。

examples.sentence: Rather than being frightened by the scale of the challenge, she saw it as a rare opportunity to prove herself.
examples.trans: 她非但没有被挑战的规模吓倒，反而将其视为证明自己的难得机会。

equality.usageZh: 名词（Noun）。常用于讨论社会、权利、机会等抽象概念。常见搭配：gender equality（性别平等）、social equality（社会平等）、racial equality（种族平等）、equality of opportunity（机会平等）。语体偏正式，常见于议论文和新闻报道。

examples.sentence: Boys and girls should have equality in the classroom.
examples.trans: 男孩和女孩在教室里应该享有平等。

examples.sentence: Our teacher always talks about equality between different groups of students.
examples.trans: 我们老师经常谈到不同学生群体之间的平等。

examples.sentence: The new law was passed to protect equality in the workplace for all employees.
examples.trans: 这项新法律通过是为了保障所有员工在工作场所的平等。

examples.sentence: Achieving true equality requires not only fair laws but also a change in people's attitudes.
examples.trans: 实现真正的平等不仅需要公正的法律，还需要人们观念的改变。

examples.sentence: The report argues that equality of opportunity, rather than equality of outcome, should be the primary goal of education policy.
examples.trans: 该报告认为，教育政策的首要目标应当是机会平等，而非结果平等。

examples.sentence: While legal frameworks have made significant progress in promoting gender equality, deeply rooted cultural norms continue to undermine these efforts in practice.
examples.trans: 尽管法律框架在促进性别平等方面取得了重大进展，但根深蒂固的文化规范仍在实践中削弱着这些努力。

inequality.usageZh: 名词（Noun）。通常指社会、经济、收入或机会上的不公平。常见搭配：economic inequality（经济不平等）、social inequality（社会不平等）、income inequality（收入不平等）、growing/widening inequality（日益加剧的不平等）。语体正式，多用于学术写作和新闻报道。

examples.sentence: There is still inequality between rich and poor people.
examples.trans: 富人和穷人之间仍然存在不平等。

examples.sentence: The report shows that inequality in education is still a big problem in some areas.
examples.trans: 报告显示，教育不平等在一些地区仍然是一个大问题。

examples.sentence: Many people are working hard to reduce inequality between cities and villages.
examples.trans: 许多人正在努力缩小城市和乡村之间的不平等。

examples.sentence: Rising income inequality has become a central concern for economists and policymakers alike.
examples.trans: 日益加剧的收入不平等已成为经济学家和政策制定者共同关注的核心问题。

examples.sentence: The study reveals a striking inequality in access to digital resources between urban and rural schools.
examples.trans: 该研究揭示了城乡学校在获取数字资源方面存在的显著不平等。

examples.sentence: Unless structural inequality is addressed at its roots, short-term welfare programs will do little to narrow the gap between the privileged and the marginalized.
examples.trans: 除非从根源上解决结构性不平等，否则短期福利项目对缩小特权群体与边缘群体之间的差距几乎无济于事。

unacceptable.usageZh: 形容词，表示“不能接受的”。常用于描述行为、态度、条件等令人无法容忍。常见句型：It is unacceptable to do sth / that 从句。语气较强，多用于正式或严肃场合。

examples.sentence: Throwing rubbish in the river is unacceptable.
examples.trans: 往河里扔垃圾是不能接受的。

examples.sentence: It is unacceptable to shout at your classmates during a group activity.
examples.trans: 在小组活动中对同学大喊大叫是不可接受的。

examples.sentence: The noise from the construction site at midnight was simply unacceptable to the nearby residents.
examples.trans: 午夜工地传来的噪音对附近居民来说简直无法接受。

examples.sentence: Given the seriousness of the mistake, the manager made it clear that such carelessness was unacceptable in this department.
examples.trans: 考虑到错误的严重性，经理明确表示这种粗心大意在这个部门是不可接受的。

examples.sentence: While minor delays can be tolerated, a complete disregard for the agreed deadline is utterly unacceptable in any professional setting.
examples.trans: 虽然轻微延误可以容忍，但完全无视约定截止日期在任何职业环境中都是完全不可接受的。

examples.sentence: The report concluded that the level of pollution in the river had reached an unacceptable threshold, posing a direct threat to public health.
examples.trans: 报告得出结论，河流的污染程度已达到不可接受的阈值，对公共健康构成直接威胁。

judging.usageZh: 动名词，来自动词 judge，表示“评判、判断”。常指基于表面或片面信息评价他人，多含贬义。常见搭配：judging by/from（根据……判断），stop judging people（停止评判他人）。

examples.sentence: Stop judging my new haircut — I like it.
examples.trans: 别再评判我的新发型了——我喜欢它。

examples.sentence: Judging people by their clothes alone often leads to wrong ideas about them.
examples.trans: 仅凭衣着评判他人往往会导致对他们的错误看法。

examples.sentence: Judging from the dark clouds, we should take umbrellas with us before leaving home.
examples.trans: 从乌云来看，我们出门前应该带上雨伞。

examples.sentence: Instead of judging the proposal too quickly, the committee decided to examine its long-term effects on the local economy.
examples.trans: 委员会没有过快地评判该提案，而是决定考察其对当地经济的长期影响。

examples.sentence: Judging a historical figure by modern moral standards often ignores the social context in which that person lived.
examples.trans: 用现代道德标准评判历史人物，往往忽略了那个人所生活的社会背景。

examples.sentence: The study warns against judging the effectiveness of an educational policy solely by short-term test scores, as deeper learning outcomes take years to emerge.
examples.trans: 该研究提醒人们不要仅凭短期考试分数来评判一项教育政策的有效性，因为更深层的学习成果需要数年才能显现。

responsible.usageZh: 形容词，表示“有责任的、负责的”。最常用结构：be responsible for (doing) sth，意为“对……负责”。也可表示“可靠的、可信赖的”，修饰人。

examples.sentence: My sister is responsible for feeding the cat every morning.
examples.trans: 我姐姐负责每天早上喂猫。

examples.sentence: As the class monitor, Tom is responsible for collecting homework before the first lesson.
examples.trans: 作为班长，汤姆负责在第一节课前收作业。

examples.sentence: Parents are responsible for teaching their children basic safety rules at home and on the road.
examples.trans: 父母有责任教孩子在家中和路上的基本安全规则。

examples.sentence: The company claims that it cannot be held responsible for damage caused by improper use of its products.
examples.trans: 该公司声称，对于因不当使用其产品而造成的损坏，它不承担责任。

examples.sentence: A truly responsible leader is one who accepts the consequences of difficult decisions rather than shifting the blame onto others.
examples.trans: 一个真正负责任的领导者，是那种承担艰难决定所带来的后果、而不是把责任推给别人的人。

examples.sentence: Researchers found that adolescents who are given age-appropriate household duties tend to grow into more responsible and self-reliant adults.
examples.trans: 研究人员发现，被赋予适龄家务责任的青少年往往成长为更有责任感、更自立的成年人。

peaceful.usageZh: 形容词，意为“和平的，安宁的”。可修饰地点、时刻、活动或心境。常见搭配：a peaceful place（宁静的地方）、a peaceful protest（和平抗议）、feel peaceful（感到平静）。

examples.sentence: The lake is peaceful in the early morning.
examples.trans: 清晨的湖面很宁静。

examples.sentence: We found a peaceful corner in the park to have our picnic.
examples.trans: 我们在公园里找了一个安静的角落野餐。

examples.sentence: The village remains peaceful even though the city nearby is very busy.
examples.trans: 尽管附近的城市很繁忙，这个村庄依然很安宁。

examples.sentence: Listening to soft music before going to bed helps create a peaceful state of mind.
examples.trans: 睡前听轻音乐有助于营造平静的心境。

examples.sentence: Unlike the crowded tourist spots, this small island offers a truly peaceful escape from daily stress.
examples.trans: 与拥挤的旅游景点不同，这座小岛为人们提供了一个真正远离日常压力的宁静去处。

examples.sentence: The two nations, after decades of conflict, finally signed a treaty that promised a peaceful resolution to their border disputes.
examples.trans: 经过数十年的冲突，这两个国家终于签署了一项条约，承诺以和平方式解决边界争端。

trust.usageZh: 可作名词或动词。作名词时常见搭配：build trust（建立信任）、mutual trust（相互信任）、have trust in sb（信任某人）。作动词时常用结构：trust sb to do sth（放心让某人做某事）、trust that...（相信……）。

examples.sentence: I trust my best friend with my secrets.
examples.trans: 我信任我最好的朋友，愿意把秘密告诉他。

examples.sentence: It takes time to build trust between new classmates.
examples.trans: 在新同学之间建立信任需要时间。

examples.sentence: You can trust Tom to keep his promise because he never lets people down.
examples.trans: 你可以放心让汤姆遵守诺言，因为他从不让人失望。

examples.sentence: Having worked together for years, the two scientists developed a deep trust in each other's judgment.
examples.trans: 经过多年合作，这两位科学家对彼此的判断建立了深厚的信任。

examples.sentence: A leader who fails to keep his word will soon find that trust, once broken, is extremely difficult to rebuild.
examples.trans: 一个不守信用的领导者很快就会发现，信任一旦破裂，极难重建。

examples.sentence: The charity's reputation for transparency has earned it the trust of donors who might otherwise hesitate to contribute.
examples.trans: 该慈善机构以透明著称，这为它赢得了那些原本可能犹豫不决的捐赠者的信任。

government.usageZh: 名词，意为“政府”。常与定冠词 the 连用，指某一特定政府。常见搭配：local government（地方政府）、central government（中央政府）、government policy（政府政策）、government official（政府官员）。

examples.sentence: The government helps build new schools in our town.
examples.trans: 政府帮助我们镇上建新学校。

examples.sentence: The local government is planning to plant more trees along the main road.
examples.trans: 当地政府正计划在主干道两旁种植更多树木。

examples.sentence: The government has passed a new law to protect wild animals in this area.
examples.trans: 政府通过了一项新法律来保护这个地区的野生动物。

examples.sentence: To reduce air pollution, the government is encouraging citizens to use public transport instead of private cars.
examples.trans: 为了减少空气污染，政府正在鼓励市民使用公共交通而不是私家车。

examples.sentence: While the government claims the new policy will boost employment, critics argue that it may place a heavier burden on small businesses.
examples.trans: 尽管政府声称新政策将促进就业，但批评者认为它可能会给小企业带来更重的负担。

examples.sentence: The government's decision to invest heavily in renewable energy reflects a long-term commitment to reducing the country's dependence on fossil fuels.
examples.trans: 政府大力投资可再生能源的决定，体现了其减少国家对化石燃料依赖的长期承诺。

suffered.usageZh: 动词 (Verb)，过去式。常用结构：suffer from + 疾病/问题，表示“遭受……之苦”。也可直接接宾语，如 suffer pain/loss。多用于描述已经发生的痛苦经历。

examples.sentence: My grandpa suffered a lot when he had a bad cold last week.
examples.trans: 我爷爷上周得重感冒时受了很多苦。

examples.sentence: The little dog suffered from hunger before a kind girl found it.
examples.trans: 那只小狗在一个善良的女孩发现它之前一直挨饿。

examples.sentence: The city suffered serious damage because the storm lasted for two days.
examples.trans: 由于暴风雨持续了两天，这座城市遭受了严重破坏。

examples.sentence: Having suffered from anxiety for years, she finally decided to ask a doctor for help.
examples.trans: 遭受焦虑困扰多年后，她终于决定向医生求助。

examples.sentence: Unlike his brother, who rarely fell ill, Tom suffered from one infection after another as a child.
examples.trans: 与他很少生病的哥哥不同，汤姆小时候一次又一次地遭受感染。

examples.sentence: The company suffered a sharp decline in profits after the new policy took effect, forcing it to cut nearly a third of its workforce.
examples.trans: 新政策生效后，该公司利润急剧下滑，被迫裁掉了近三分之一的员工。

depressed.usageZh: 形容词 (Adjective)。描述情绪低落、消沉的状态。常用搭配：feel depressed, look depressed, become depressed。口语和书面语均可使用，但语气比 sad 更重。

examples.sentence: Lucy felt depressed because her best friend moved to another city.
examples.trans: 露西因为最好的朋友搬去了另一个城市而感到沮丧。

examples.sentence: The long rainy days made everyone in our class feel a little depressed.
examples.trans: 漫长的雨天让我们班每个人都感到有点消沉。

examples.sentence: He became depressed after his dog died, so his parents bought him a new puppy.
examples.trans: 他的狗死后他变得很沮丧，所以他父母给他买了一只新的小狗。

examples.sentence: Feeling depressed for weeks, she stopped answering phone calls and refused to leave her room.
examples.trans: 连续几周感到抑郁后，她不再接电话，也拒绝离开自己的房间。

examples.sentence: Although he appeared cheerful in public, he admitted in his diary that he had never felt so depressed in his life.
examples.trans: 尽管他在公共场合显得很开朗，但他在日记中承认自己一生中从未感到如此抑郁。

examples.sentence: Prolonged sleep deprivation has been shown to leave even healthy adults feeling depressed and unable to concentrate on routine tasks.
examples.trans: 长期睡眠不足已被证明会让健康的成年人也感到抑郁，并且无法集中精力完成日常任务。

contribution.usageZh: 名词 (Noun)。常用短语：make a contribution to（为……做贡献），其中 to 为介词，后接名词或动名词。也可表示“捐款”或“稿件”。正式程度中等，书面和口语都常用。

examples.sentence: My mom made a big contribution to our school food sale by baking 50 cakes.
examples.trans: 我妈妈烤了50个蛋糕，为我们学校的食品义卖做了很大贡献。

examples.sentence: Every student's contribution to the class project helped make it a success.
examples.trans: 每个学生对班级项目的贡献都帮助它取得了成功。

examples.sentence: The scientist won a national award for her contribution to cancer research.
examples.trans: 这位科学家因对癌症研究的贡献获得了国家奖项。

examples.sentence: By volunteering at the local library every weekend, he has made a lasting contribution to the community.
examples.trans: 通过每个周末在当地图书馆做志愿者，他对社区做出了持久的贡献。

examples.sentence: While financial support is valuable, the contribution of time and professional skills often proves far more significant in the long run.
examples.trans: 虽然资金支持很有价值，但从长远来看，时间和专业技能的贡献往往更为重要。

examples.sentence: The historian's most enduring contribution lies not in the documents she uncovered but in the analytical framework she developed for interpreting them.
examples.trans: 这位历史学家最持久的贡献不在于她发现的文献，而在于她为解读这些文献所建立的分析框架。

influence.usageZh: 名词或动词。作名词时常用 have an influence on 表示“对……有影响”；作动词时直接跟宾语 influence sb/sth。名词可受 great, strong, positive, negative 等修饰。

examples.sentence: My big brother has a good influence on me.
examples.trans: 我哥哥对我有好的影响。

examples.sentence: The weather can influence how we feel every day.
examples.trans: 天气会影响我们每天的感受。

examples.sentence: Friends can influence your choices more than you realize.
examples.trans: 朋友对你的选择的影响可能比你意识到的更大。

examples.sentence: Teachers influence not only what students learn but also how they think.
examples.trans: 教师不仅影响学生学习的内容，也影响他们思考的方式。

examples.sentence: The influence of social media on teenagers has become a topic of heated debate.
examples.trans: 社交媒体对青少年的影响已成为一个热议话题。

examples.sentence: A leader's true influence is measured not by the orders they give, but by the trust they inspire.
examples.trans: 一个领导者真正的影响力不是由他下达的命令来衡量，而是由他所激发的信任来衡量。

wealthy.usageZh: 形容词，描述人、家庭、地区或国家拥有大量财富。比较级 wealthier，最高级 wealthiest。可作定语或表语，也可与 the 连用表示“富人”这一类人。

examples.sentence: The wealthy man bought a big house near the sea.
examples.trans: 那个有钱人在海边买了一栋大房子。

examples.sentence: She comes from a wealthy family, but she never shows off.
examples.trans: 她来自一个富裕家庭，但从不炫耀。

examples.sentence: Some wealthy people choose to give away most of their money to help others.
examples.trans: 一些富有的人选择捐出大部分钱来帮助别人。

examples.sentence: Being wealthy does not automatically guarantee a happy and meaningful life.
examples.trans: 富有并不自动保证幸福而有意义的生活。

examples.sentence: While the country grew wealthier overall, the gap between rich and poor continued to widen.
examples.trans: 尽管这个国家整体上变得更富裕了，但贫富差距继续扩大。

examples.sentence: A society that values only the wealthy risks overlooking the contributions of those who work behind the scenes.
examples.trans: 一个只重视富人的社会，可能会忽视那些在幕后默默付出的人的贡献。

limit.usageZh: 动词 (Verb) 或名词 (Noun)。作动词：limit something，表示“限制某物”。作名词：set a limit，表示“设定限制”。常用短语：speed limit (限速)、time limit (时间限制)。

examples.sentence: There is a speed limit near our school.
examples.trans: 我们学校附近有速度限制。

examples.sentence: My mom limits my time on the phone to one hour a day.
examples.trans: 我妈妈把我每天玩手机的时间限制在一小时以内。

examples.sentence: You should set a limit on how much money you spend each week.
examples.trans: 你应该给自己每周花多少钱设定一个限制。

examples.sentence: The number of participants is limited to thirty, so sign up early.
examples.trans: 参加人数限制在三十人以内，所以请尽早报名。

examples.sentence: While technology expands what we can do, it does not remove the limits of human energy and attention.
examples.trans: 虽然技术扩展了我们能做的事情，但它并没有消除人类精力和注意力的限制。

examples.sentence: Governments often impose strict limits on carbon emissions to slow down climate change.
examples.trans: 各国政府常常对碳排放施加严格限制，以减缓气候变化。

fundamental.usageZh: 形容词 (Adjective)。用于描述最重要、最基础的部分。常用搭配：fundamental rights (基本权利)、fundamental principles (基本原则)、fundamental change (根本性变化)。语体偏正式，常见于议论文和说明文。

examples.sentence: Learning to read is a fundamental skill.
examples.trans: 学会阅读是一项基本技能。

examples.sentence: Trust is fundamental to a good friendship.
examples.trans: 信任对一段好的友谊来说是根本的。

examples.sentence: There is a fundamental difference between wanting something and needing it.
examples.trans: 想要某样东西和需要某样东西之间有一个根本的区别。

examples.sentence: Understanding basic grammar is fundamental to writing clear English sentences.
examples.trans: 理解基本语法是写出清晰英语句子的基础。

examples.sentence: The report argues that access to clean water is a fundamental human right, not a privilege.
examples.trans: 该报告认为，获得清洁水源是一项基本人权，而不是一种特权。

examples.sentence: A fundamental shift in public attitudes toward recycling is required if the city is to meet its waste-reduction targets.
examples.trans: 如果该市要实现其减少废物的目标，公众对回收利用的态度就需要发生根本性转变。

expression.usageZh: 名词 (Noun)。有两个主要含义：1. 表达思想或感情（抽象），如 freedom of expression (言论自由)。2. 面部表情（具体），如 a happy expression (开心的表情)。常用搭配：facial expression (面部表情)、idiomatic expression (习语表达)。

examples.sentence: She had a happy expression on her face.
examples.trans: 她脸上带着开心的表情。

examples.sentence: Drawing is a good way of expression for young children.
examples.trans: 画画是幼儿表达的一种好方式。

examples.sentence: The teacher asked us to explain the expression in our own words.
examples.trans: 老师让我们用自己的话解释这个表达。

examples.sentence: Freedom of expression is protected by law in many democratic countries.
examples.trans: 在许多民主国家，言论自由受到法律保护。

examples.sentence: His facial expression remained calm even when the results were announced, revealing nothing about his true feelings.
examples.trans: 即使结果公布时，他的面部表情依然平静，没有流露出任何真实情绪。

examples.sentence: The novel is admired not only for its plot but also for the precision and beauty of its verbal expression.
examples.trans: 这部小说之所以受到赞赏，不仅因为其情节，还因为其语言表达的精确与优美。

jealous of.usageZh: 形容词短语，后接名词或代词作宾语。口语和书面语都常用，表示羡慕或嫉妒某人/某物。注意不要与 envious of 混淆，jealous 语气更重，常带有不安或不满的情绪。

examples.sentence: My little brother is jealous of my new bike.
examples.trans: 我弟弟嫉妒我的新自行车。

examples.sentence: She felt jealous of her classmate who always got higher marks in maths.
examples.trans: 她嫉妒那个数学总是考得更高的同班同学。

examples.sentence: He tried not to feel jealous of his cousin, who had just won a national speech contest.
examples.trans: 他努力不让自己嫉妒刚在全国演讲比赛中获奖的表哥。

examples.sentence: Having grown up in a large family, she never learned to be jealous of others' attention from their parents.
examples.trans: 在一个大家庭中长大，她从未学会去嫉妒别人从父母那里得到的关注。

examples.sentence: Rather than feeling jealous of her colleague's promotion, she chose to analyze what skills she still needed to develop.
examples.trans: 她没有嫉妒同事的升职，而是选择分析自己还需要培养哪些技能。

examples.sentence: A mature person may acknowledge being jealous of a friend's achievement, yet still offer genuine congratulations without letting envy damage the relationship.
examples.trans: 一个成熟的人也许会承认自己嫉妒朋友的成就，但仍会真诚地表示祝贺，不让这份嫉妒破坏彼此的关系。

broke up with.usageZh: 动词短语，break up with 的过去式形式。后接表示人的名词或代词作宾语，指结束恋爱关系。口语中极为常用，也可用于较随意的书面叙述。注意与 break up（不及物，表示"分手"或"散会"）区分。

examples.sentence: Tom broke up with his girlfriend last week.
examples.trans: 汤姆上周和女朋友分手了。

examples.sentence: She broke up with him after she found out he had lied about his age.
examples.trans: 她发现他谎报年龄后就和他分手了。

examples.sentence: Although they had been together for three years, they finally broke up with each other because they wanted different things in life.
examples.trans: 尽管他们在一起三年了，但最终还是因为人生追求不同而分手了。

examples.sentence: Having realized that their long-distance relationship was causing more stress than happiness, she decided to break up with him before the new semester began.
examples.trans: 意识到异地恋带来的压力大于快乐后，她决定在新学期开始前和他分手。

examples.sentence: He never expected that she would break up with him over a minor disagreement, which made him reflect on how poorly he had handled their conflicts.
examples.trans: 他从没想过她会因为一次小分歧就和他分手，这让他反思自己处理矛盾的方式有多糟糕。

examples.sentence: It is often more painful to be the one who is broken up with than the one who initiates the breakup, yet both sides need time to heal and move forward.
examples.trans: 被分手的一方往往比主动提出分手的一方更痛苦，但双方都需要时间来疗愈并继续前行。

get over.usageZh: 动词短语，后接名词、代词或动名词作宾语。表示从疾病、悲伤、失望等不愉快经历中恢复过来。口语和书面语都常用。否定形式 can't get over 常表示"难以置信"或"无法释怀"。

family.meaning: 恢复；克服（较少单独使用）

examples.sentence: It took me a week to get over my cold.
examples.trans: 我花了一周时间才从感冒中恢复过来。

examples.sentence: He still hasn't got over losing the football match last month.
examples.trans: 他还没有从上个月输掉足球比赛的阴影中走出来。

examples.sentence: After failing the driving test twice, she needed some time to get over her disappointment before trying again.
examples.trans: 两次驾照考试失败后，她需要一些时间来克服失望情绪，然后再试一次。

examples.sentence: It is not easy to get over the fear of public speaking, but with regular practice and positive feedback, most people can gradually overcome it.
examples.trans: 克服公开演讲的恐惧并不容易，但通过定期练习和积极反馈，大多数人可以逐渐战胜它。

examples.sentence: Unlike physical injuries, emotional wounds often take much longer to get over, especially when the person refuses to talk about what happened.
examples.trans: 与身体上的伤不同，情感上的创伤往往需要更长时间才能愈合，尤其是当当事人拒绝谈论所发生的事情时。

examples.sentence: The ability to get over setbacks quickly, rather than the absence of failure itself, is what distinguishes resilient individuals from those who give up at the first sign of difficulty.
examples.trans: 快速从挫折中恢复的能力——而非从未失败——才是坚韧者与那些一遇困难就放弃的人之间的区别所在。

stand their ground.usageZh: 动词短语，主语通常是人或团体。用于描述在争论、压力或威胁下保持坚定，不改变立场。常见搭配：refuse to stand their ground, be willing to stand their ground。口语和书面语均可使用。

examples.sentence: My little brother wanted my toy, but I stood my ground and kept it.
examples.trans: 我弟弟想要我的玩具，但我坚持立场，没有给他。

examples.sentence: When the whole class laughed at her idea, she stood her ground and explained it again.
examples.trans: 当全班嘲笑她的想法时，她坚持立场，又解释了一遍。

examples.sentence: Although the seller kept lowering the price, my mother stood her ground and refused to buy the damaged bag.
examples.trans: 尽管卖家不断降价，我妈妈还是坚持立场，拒绝买那个有破损的包。

examples.sentence: Facing strong opposition from the school board, the student council stood their ground and insisted on holding the charity event.
examples.trans: 面对校董事会的强烈反对，学生会坚持立场，执意举办慈善活动。

examples.sentence: Rather than giving in to the unreasonable demands, the negotiator chose to stand her ground, which ultimately earned her the respect of both sides.
examples.trans: 谈判者没有屈服于不合理的要求，而是选择坚持立场，这最终为她赢得了双方的尊重。

examples.sentence: In the face of mounting criticism from the media, the scientist stood his ground, arguing that the data, however inconvenient, could not be ignored.
examples.trans: 面对媒体日益激烈的批评，这位科学家坚持立场，认为这些数据无论多么令人难堪，都不能被忽视。

come to a common understanding.usageZh: 动词短语，'come to' 表示“达成、达到”，后接 'a common understanding'。主语通常是双方或多方。常用于会议、谈判、家庭沟通等正式或半正式语境。

examples.sentence: After talking for ten minutes, my friend and I came to a common understanding about which game to play.
examples.trans: 聊了十分钟后，我和朋友就玩哪个游戏达成了共识。

examples.sentence: The two groups argued for a while, but they finally came to a common understanding about sharing the playground.
examples.trans: 两个小组争论了一会儿，但最终就共用操场达成了共识。

examples.sentence: Before starting the group project, we discussed our ideas carefully so that we could come to a common understanding of the task.
examples.trans: 在开始小组项目之前，我们仔细讨论了各自的想法，以便对任务达成共识。

examples.sentence: After several rounds of negotiation, the two companies came to a common understanding regarding the distribution of profits.
examples.trans: 经过几轮谈判，两家公司就利润分配达成了共识。

examples.sentence: It took the committee nearly three hours to come to a common understanding, as each member had a fundamentally different vision for the project.
examples.trans: 委员会花了将近三个小时才达成共识，因为每位成员对项目的设想都截然不同。

examples.sentence: Only when both parties are willing to set aside their prejudices can they come to a common understanding that serves the long-term interests of the community.
examples.trans: 只有当双方都愿意放下偏见时，他们才能达成符合社区长远利益的共识。

live in peace.usageZh: 动词短语，'live' 为不及物动词，'in peace' 作状语。用于描述个人、家庭、社群或国家之间没有冲突、安宁共处的状态。常见搭配：live in peace with sb, learn to live in peace。

examples.sentence: My cat and my dog sleep together and live in peace.
examples.trans: 我的猫和狗睡在一起，和平相处。

examples.sentence: After the big fight, the two brothers said sorry and promised to live in peace from then on.
examples.trans: 大吵一架之后，两兄弟互相道歉，并承诺从此以后和平相处。

examples.sentence: People from different cultures can live in peace if they respect each other's customs and beliefs.
examples.trans: 如果不同文化背景的人互相尊重彼此的习俗和信仰，他们就能和平共处。

examples.sentence: The villagers, regardless of their religious differences, have learned to live in peace and support one another during difficult times.
examples.trans: 村民们尽管宗教信仰不同，但已经学会和平共处，并在困难时期互相帮助。

examples.sentence: History teaches us that nations cannot truly live in peace unless they address the underlying causes of conflict rather than merely suppressing them.
examples.trans: 历史告诉我们，除非各国解决冲突的根本原因而不仅仅是压制冲突，否则无法真正和平共处。

examples.sentence: The treaty was signed not merely to end the war, but to establish a framework within which former enemies could live in peace and rebuild their shattered economies.
examples.trans: 签署该条约不仅是为了结束战争，更是为了建立一个框架，使昔日的敌人能够和平共处并重建他们破碎的经济。

went through.usageZh: 动词短语，后接名词或名词短语。通常用于描述经历困难时期、变化或过程。口语和书面语都常见，但更偏向于叙述已经发生的事情。

examples.sentence: My grandpa went through a hard winter last year.
examples.trans: 我爷爷去年经历了一个难熬的冬天。

examples.sentence: She went through a lot of old photos and found one of her mother.
examples.trans: 她翻看了很多旧照片，找到了一张她妈妈的照片。

examples.sentence: The city went through great changes after the new railway was built.
examples.trans: 新铁路建成后，这座城市经历了巨大的变化。

examples.sentence: Having gone through several interviews, he finally got the job he had always wanted.
examples.trans: 经历了几次面试之后，他终于得到了那份一直想要的工作。

examples.sentence: The company went through a painful restructuring, yet it emerged stronger than before.
examples.trans: 公司经历了一次痛苦的重组，但之后却变得比以前更强大。

examples.sentence: Anyone who has gone through the loss of a close friend understands how long the healing process can take.
examples.trans: 任何经历过失去挚友之痛的人都明白，愈合的过程有多么漫长。

keep in mind.usageZh: 动词短语，后接 that 从句或名词短语。用于提醒某人记住重要信息或考虑某个因素。口语和书面语都常用，语气比 remember 更强调“放在心上”。

examples.sentence: Keep in mind that the bus leaves at seven.
examples.trans: 记住，公交车七点开。

examples.sentence: When you ride a bike, keep in mind that the road can be wet after rain.
examples.trans: 骑自行车时，要记住雨后路面可能会湿。

examples.sentence: Keep in mind that every choice you make now will affect your future.
examples.trans: 要记住，你现在做的每一个选择都会影响你的未来。

examples.sentence: While planning the school trip, we must keep in mind that not all students can afford expensive activities.
examples.trans: 在计划学校旅行时，我们必须考虑到并非所有学生都能负担得起昂贵的活动。

examples.sentence: It is essential to keep in mind that short-term gains should never be pursued at the cost of long-term stability.
examples.trans: 必须牢记，绝不能以牺牲长期稳定为代价来追求短期利益。

examples.sentence: When evaluating historical figures, one should keep in mind that their actions were shaped by the values of their own time.
examples.trans: 在评价历史人物时，应当记住他们的行为受到其所处时代价值观的塑造。

would rather.usageZh: 情态动词短语，后接动词原形。用于表达偏好或选择，常与 than 连用表示“宁愿……也不愿……”。口语和书面语都常见，语气比 prefer 更主观。

examples.sentence: I would rather have noodles than rice today.
examples.trans: 今天我想吃面条，不想吃米饭。

examples.sentence: My sister would rather walk to school than take the crowded bus.
examples.trans: 我妹妹宁愿走路上学，也不愿坐拥挤的公交车。

examples.sentence: He would rather stay at home and finish his project than go out with friends.
examples.trans: 他宁愿待在家里完成项目，也不愿和朋友出去。

examples.sentence: Many teenagers would rather communicate through text messages than talk face to face.
examples.trans: 许多青少年宁愿通过短信交流，也不愿面对面交谈。

examples.sentence: She would rather risk failure by trying something new than remain trapped in a job she dislikes.
examples.trans: 她宁愿冒着失败的风险去尝试新事物，也不愿困在自己不喜欢的工作里。

examples.sentence: Given the choice between a high salary and meaningful work, an increasing number of graduates say they would rather pursue the latter.
examples.trans: 在高薪和有意义的工作之间做选择时，越来越多的毕业生表示他们宁愿追求后者。

on-line dating.usageZh: 名词短语，不可数。'on-line'（或 online）修饰 'dating'，表示通过互联网寻找和建立恋爱关系。常作主语、宾语或定语，如 on-line dating sites（交友网站）。语体偏现代生活话题，口语和书面语均可用。

examples.sentence: My sister met her boyfriend through on-line dating.
examples.trans: 我姐姐是通过网上约会认识她男朋友的。

examples.sentence: On-line dating is quite common among young people in big cities.
examples.trans: 在大城市里，网上约会在年轻人中相当普遍。

examples.sentence: Although on-line dating saves time, you still need to be careful about whom you talk to.
examples.trans: 虽然网上约会节省时间，但你仍然需要小心和谁聊天。

examples.sentence: Having tried on-line dating for several months, she realized that face-to-face meetings reveal much more about a person.
examples.trans: 尝试了几个月网上约会后，她意识到面对面的见面能让人了解更多关于一个人的信息。

examples.sentence: Unlike traditional matchmaking, on-line dating allows individuals to filter potential partners by interests and values before committing to a meeting.
examples.trans: 与传统的媒人介绍不同，网上约会允许个人在决定见面之前，按照兴趣和价值观筛选潜在伴侣。

examples.sentence: The rapid expansion of on-line dating has reshaped modern courtship, yet it also raises concerns about privacy and the authenticity of self-presentation.
examples.trans: 网上约会的迅速扩张重塑了现代求爱方式，但同时也引发了人们对隐私以及自我呈现真实性的担忧。

as equal as.usageZh: 比较结构，表示两者在地位、价值或权利上同等。常见结构：A + be + as equal as + B。多用于正式或议论性语境，强调平等关系。注意 equal 本身已有“平等”含义，as equal as 带有强调语气。

examples.sentence: In our class, boys and girls are as equal as each other.
examples.trans: 在我们班上，男生和女生彼此一样平等。

examples.sentence: The teacher said that every student's opinion is as equal as anyone else's.
examples.trans: 老师说每个学生的意见和其他任何人的意见一样平等。

examples.sentence: In a healthy friendship, both sides should feel as equal as possible.
examples.trans: 在一段健康的友谊中，双方都应该尽可能感到平等。

examples.sentence: The new policy ensures that part-time workers are treated as equal as full-time employees in terms of basic rights.
examples.trans: 新政策确保兼职工作者在基本权利方面与全职员工受到同等对待。

examples.sentence: A society cannot claim to be just unless every citizen, regardless of background, is regarded as equal as the next before the law.
examples.trans: 除非每个公民无论背景如何，在法律面前都被视为与其他人一样平等，否则一个社会就不能自称公正。

examples.sentence: The principle that all member states should be as equal as one another in decision-making remains fundamental to the organization's legitimacy.
examples.trans: 所有成员国在决策中应彼此平等的原则，仍然是该组织合法性的根本所在。

came from.usageZh: 动词短语，过去式，原形为 come from。表示来源、出身或起因，后接名词或名词短语。可用于人（来自某地）、事物（来源于某物）或观念（起源于某处）。口语和书面语均常用。

examples.sentence: My best friend came from a small town near the sea.
examples.trans: 我最好的朋友来自海边的一个小镇。

examples.sentence: The idea for the school project came from a science magazine.
examples.trans: 这个学校项目的想法来自一本科学杂志。

examples.sentence: The tradition of giving red envelopes came from ancient China.
examples.trans: 发红包的传统来源于古代中国。

examples.sentence: Much of the confusion came from a lack of clear communication between the two departments.
examples.trans: 大部分混乱源于两个部门之间缺乏清晰的沟通。

examples.sentence: Her passion for environmental protection came from years of witnessing pollution in her hometown.
examples.trans: 她对环境保护的热情来源于多年来目睹家乡污染的经历。

examples.sentence: The architectural style of the building came from a blend of Eastern and Western influences, reflecting the city's colonial history.
examples.trans: 这座建筑的风格来源于东西方影响的融合，反映了这座城市的殖民历史。

up to.usageZh: 介词短语，表示“由……决定”或“取决于”，常用结构为“It is up to someone to do something”，意为“做某事是某人的责任/由某人决定”。口语和书面语都常见，语气中性偏正式。

examples.sentence: It is up to you to choose the color.
examples.trans: 选什么颜色由你决定。

examples.sentence: Whether we take the bus or walk is up to my dad.
examples.trans: 我们坐公交还是走路由我爸爸决定。

examples.sentence: It is up to each student to keep the classroom clean.
examples.trans: 保持教室整洁是每个学生的责任。

examples.sentence: It is up to the manager to decide whether the project should continue.
examples.trans: 这个项目是否继续由经理决定。

examples.sentence: Ultimately, it is up to individuals to take responsibility for their own health.
examples.trans: 归根结底，个人要为自己的健康负责。

examples.sentence: Given the complexity of the issue, it is up to the committee to weigh the potential risks before reaching a conclusion.
examples.trans: 鉴于问题的复杂性，委员会需要在得出结论前权衡潜在风险。

fill the gap.usageZh: 动词短语，意为“填补空白、弥补差距”，常与“by”连用表示方式，也可接“between A and B”表示填补两者之间的差距。可用于谈论知识、服务、资源、代际等差距。

examples.sentence: The new books fill the gap on the shelf.
examples.trans: 新书填补了书架上的空位。

examples.sentence: After-school clubs help fill the gap between school and home time.
examples.trans: 课后社团帮助填补放学和回家之间的时间空档。

examples.sentence: The government is building new schools to fill the gap in rural education.
examples.trans: 政府正在建新学校来弥补农村教育的不足。

examples.sentence: Online courses can fill the gap for students who lack access to quality teachers.
examples.trans: 在线课程可以弥补那些无法获得优质教师资源的学生的不足。

examples.sentence: The charity aims to fill the gap between rich and poor communities by providing equal learning opportunities.
examples.trans: 该慈善机构旨在通过提供平等的学习机会来缩小贫富社区之间的差距。

examples.sentence: To fill the gap left by the sudden departure of the team leader, the company promoted an experienced engineer from within.
examples.trans: 为了填补团队负责人突然离职留下的空缺，公司从内部提拔了一位经验丰富的工程师。

suffer from.usageZh: 动词短语，后接名词，表示“遭受……之苦”或“患有……疾病”，常用于描述健康问题、心理压力、社会问题等。语体偏正式，但在日常口语中也常见。

examples.sentence: My grandpa suffers from a bad back.
examples.trans: 我爷爷背疼得厉害。

examples.sentence: Many students suffer from a lack of sleep during exam week.
examples.trans: 考试周期间，许多学生睡眠不足。

examples.sentence: People in dry areas often suffer from a shortage of clean water.
examples.trans: 干旱地区的人们常常缺乏干净的饮用水。

examples.sentence: Children who suffer from anxiety may find it hard to concentrate in class.
examples.trans: 患有焦虑症的儿童可能很难在课堂上集中注意力。

examples.sentence: Unlike their urban peers, students in remote villages often suffer from limited access to digital resources.
examples.trans: 与城市同龄人不同，偏远乡村的学生常常苦于数字资源有限。

examples.sentence: The region has long suffered from economic stagnation, which has in turn worsened the outflow of young talent.
examples.trans: 该地区长期遭受经济停滞之苦，这反过来又加剧了年轻人才的流失。

go together.usageZh: 动词短语，常与 with 连用，表示“与……紧密相连”或“相伴发生”。也可单独使用，表示两件事或两个人经常一起出现。口语和书面语均可使用，书面语中更常见于议论或说明性文字。

examples.sentence: Milk and cookies go together very well.
examples.trans: 牛奶和饼干搭配起来很好吃。

examples.sentence: Rain and dark clouds often go together in summer.
examples.trans: 夏天，雨和乌云常常一起出现。

examples.sentence: A healthy diet usually goes together with regular exercise.
examples.trans: 健康的饮食通常与规律的运动相伴。

examples.sentence: Economic growth does not always go together with social progress.
examples.trans: 经济增长并不总是与社会进步同步。

examples.sentence: In many cultures, hospitality goes together with a strong sense of community.
examples.trans: 在许多文化中，热情好客与强烈的社区意识密不可分。

examples.sentence: The report argues that political stability goes together with the protection of fundamental rights, rather than being achieved at their expense.
examples.trans: 该报告认为，政治稳定与基本权利的保护相辅相成，而非以牺牲基本权利为代价。

such as.usageZh: 用于列举例子，放在所举例子的前面，意为“例如，比如”。通常引出两个或以上的例子，不用逗号与前面的名词隔开。口语和书面语中都很常见，比 for example 更紧凑。

examples.sentence: I like fruits such as apples and bananas.
examples.trans: 我喜欢水果，比如苹果和香蕉。

examples.sentence: We can do many things on weekends, such as riding bikes or reading books.
examples.trans: 我们周末可以做很多事情，比如骑自行车或读书。

examples.sentence: Some subjects, such as physics and chemistry, require careful observation.
examples.trans: 有些学科，比如物理和化学，需要仔细观察。

examples.sentence: Renewable energy sources, such as wind and solar power, are becoming more affordable.
examples.trans: 可再生能源，如风能和太阳能，正变得越来越便宜。

examples.sentence: Soft skills, such as effective communication and teamwork, are highly valued by employers across industries.
examples.trans: 软技能，如有效沟通和团队合作，受到各行各业雇主的高度重视。

examples.sentence: Historical evidence suggests that civilizations decline when core institutions, such as the legal system and public education, fail to adapt to changing circumstances.
examples.trans: 历史证据表明，当核心制度（如法律体系和公共教育）未能适应变化的环境时，文明就会衰落。

according to.usageZh: 介词短语，后接名词、代词或名词性短语，表示“根据、按照”。常用于引出信息来源、规则或某种标准。口语和书面语都常用，正式程度中等。

examples.sentence: According to my mom, this soup is good for a cold.
examples.trans: 据我妈妈说，这种汤对感冒有好处。

examples.sentence: According to the school rules, we must wear uniforms on Mondays.
examples.trans: 根据学校规定，我们周一必须穿校服。

examples.sentence: According to the map, the museum is just around the corner.
examples.trans: 根据地图，博物馆就在拐角处。

examples.sentence: According to a recent survey, most teenagers spend over three hours a day on their phones.
examples.trans: 根据最近的一项调查，大多数青少年每天花在手机上的时间超过三小时。

examples.sentence: According to the report, the new policy has significantly reduced traffic jams in the city center.
examples.trans: 根据该报告，新政策已显著减少了市中心的交通拥堵。

examples.sentence: According to the data collected over a five-year period, the species has gradually adapted to the changing climate.
examples.trans: 根据五年间收集的数据，该物种已逐渐适应了不断变化的气候。

get rid of.usageZh: 动词短语，后接名词或动名词作宾语，表示“摆脱、除去、处理掉”。可用于具体物品，也可用于抽象事物如习惯、情绪、问题等。口语和书面语都常用。

examples.sentence: I need to get rid of these old toys.
examples.trans: 我需要把这些旧玩具处理掉。

examples.sentence: She opened the window to get rid of the smell of paint.
examples.trans: 她打开窗户，想散掉油漆味。

examples.sentence: He started jogging every morning to get rid of his stress.
examples.trans: 他开始每天早晨慢跑，以消除压力。

examples.sentence: The city is trying to get rid of illegal parking by introducing stricter fines.
examples.trans: 该市正试图通过实行更严格的罚款来消除违章停车现象。

examples.sentence: Getting rid of outdated equipment is the first step toward modernizing the laboratory.
examples.trans: 淘汰过时设备是实验室现代化的第一步。

examples.sentence: To get rid of the misunderstanding that had lasted for years, both sides agreed to hold an open discussion.
examples.trans: 为了消除持续多年的误解，双方同意举行一次公开讨论。

bring up.usageZh: 动词短语，后接表示人的名词或代词作宾语，意为“抚养、养育、教育”。也可表示“提出（话题）”，但本词表主要取“抚养”义。常用于谈论家庭教育和成长背景。

examples.sentence: My aunt helped bring up my cousin.
examples.trans: 我姑姑帮忙抚养了我的表弟。

examples.sentence: He was brought up by his grandparents in a small village.
examples.trans: 他是由祖父母在一个小村庄里抚养长大的。

examples.sentence: Parents should bring up their children to respect others.
examples.trans: 父母应该教育孩子尊重他人。

examples.sentence: Being brought up in a bilingual family gave her a natural advantage in learning languages.
examples.trans: 在双语家庭中长大使她在语言学习方面具有天然优势。

examples.sentence: Children brought up with a strong sense of responsibility tend to become more reliable adults.
examples.trans: 在强烈责任感中长大的孩子往往能成为更可靠的成年人。

examples.sentence: The way a child is brought up has a lasting impact on their ability to form healthy relationships later in life.
examples.trans: 孩子的成长方式对其日后建立健康人际关系的能力有着持久的影响。

grammar.key: Present Perfect Tense / 现在完成时
grammar.title: 现在完成时：从基础到高考拓展（含 since / for / already / yet / just / ever / never / recently）
grammar.titleEn: Present Perfect Tense: Core Uses and Senior High Extensions
grammar.usage:
现在完成时的核心结构是“have/has + 过去分词”。它主要用来表达两类含义：一是过去发生的动作对现在造成了影响或结果，说话时更关注现在的状态；二是动作或状态从过去开始，一直持续到现在，并且有可能继续持续下去。肯定句用“主语 + have/has + 过去分词”，否定句在 have/has 后加 not，疑问句把 have/has 提到主语之前。

在初中阶段，现在完成时通常只要求掌握“已经做完某事”“曾经做过某事”以及“持续一段时间”的基本用法，常与 already、yet、just、ever、never、before 等词连用。到了高中阶段，现在完成时的使用更加灵活，常与 since、for、recently、so far、up to now、in the last/past few years 等时间状语搭配，并且需要区分现在完成时与一般过去时、现在完成进行时的语用差异。

现在完成时与一般过去时最大的区别在于：一般过去时只陈述过去某个具体时间发生的动作，与现在没有直接联系；而现在完成时强调过去动作与现在的关联。例如“I lost my key yesterday.”只是说昨天丢了钥匙，而“I have lost my key.”则强调现在钥匙不见了，影响仍然存在。另一个容易混淆的是现在完成时与现在完成进行时：前者更强调结果或完成，后者更强调动作的持续性和进行感，如“I have read this book.”强调已经读完，而“I have been reading this book.”强调一直在读，不一定读完。

易错点一：现在完成时不能与表示具体过去时间的状语连用，如 yesterday、last week、two days ago、in 2019 等，这些时间状语应搭配一般过去时。易错点二：since 后面接过去的时间点或一般过去时的从句，而 for 后面接一段时间，两者不能混用。易错点三：have been to、have gone to、have been in 三者含义不同：have been to 表示“去过某地（已回来）”，have gone to 表示“去了某地（还没回来）”，have been in 表示“在某地待了多久”。易错点四：在书面语和高考语法填空中，要注意短暂性动词（如 come、go、leave、buy、borrow、die、join）不能与表示一段时间的 for/since 连用，需要转换为延续性表达，如 buy→have、borrow→keep、leave→be away、die→be dead、join→be in/be a member of。
forms: 肯定句：主语 + have/has + 过去分词（+ 其他）
否定句：主语 + have/has + not + 过去分词（+ 其他）
一般疑问句：Have/Has + 主语 + 过去分词（+ 其他）？
特殊疑问句：疑问词 + have/has + 主语 + 过去分词（+ 其他）？
since + 过去时间点 / 一般过去时从句；for + 一段时间
have been to / have gone to / have been in 的区分结构
notes: 现在完成时不能与 yesterday、last night、two days ago、in 2020 等具体过去时间连用，高考语法填空常在此设空。
since 后接时间点或一般过去时从句，for 后接时间段；若主句用现在完成时，since 从句用一般过去时。
短暂性动词不能与 for/since 表示一段时间的状语连用，高考书面表达中需转换为延续性动词或状态表达。
have been to 表示“去过某地已回来”，have gone to 表示“去了某地未回来”，have been in 表示“在某地待了多久”，高考单选和完形中常考。
在正式书面语中，现在完成时常与 so far、up to now、in recent years、over the past decade 等搭配，体现动作从过去到现在的累积或变化。

examples.en: I have already finished my homework.
examples.cn: 我已经完成了作业。

examples.en: She has lived here for five years.
examples.cn: 她在这里已经住了五年。

examples.en: Have you ever been to Beijing?
examples.cn: 你曾经去过北京吗？

examples.en: He has gone to Shanghai, so you can't find him in the office now.
examples.cn: 他已经去上海了，所以你现在在办公室找不到他。

examples.en: Great changes have taken place in our city since 2015.
examples.cn: 自2015年以来，我们的城市发生了巨大的变化。

examples.en: In recent years, the government has taken effective measures to reduce air pollution.
examples.cn: 近年来，政府已经采取了有效措施来减少空气污染。

exercises.q: I ______ my homework already.
exercises.explain: already 是现在完成时的标志词，表示已经完成。

exercises.q: She ______ to Beijing twice.
exercises.explain: twice 表示经历，用现在完成时 has been。

exercises.q: They ______ each other for three years.
exercises.explain: for three years 表示持续到现在，用现在完成时。

exercises.q: My brother ______ just ______ the room.
exercises.explain: just 是现在完成时标志词，结构为 has + 过去分词。

exercises.q: ______ you ever ______ a tiger?
exercises.explain: ever 用于现在完成时疑问句，表示曾经是否做过某事。

exercises.q: We ______ (live) in this city since 2018.
exercises.explain: since 2018 表示从过去持续到现在，用现在完成时。

exercises.q: He ______ (not finish) his lunch yet.
exercises.explain: yet 用于现在完成时否定句，表示还没完成。

exercises.q: ______ you ______ (see) my keys? I can't find them.
exercises.explain: 询问是否见过某物且对现在有影响，用现在完成时。

exercises.q: I have seen this movie yesterday.
exercises.explain: yesterday 是具体过去时间，应用一般过去时 saw。

exercises.q: She has never been to Shanghai.
exercises.explain: never 用于现在完成时，表示从未去过，句子正确。

exercises.q: I have eaten breakfast. (改为否定句)
exercises.explain: 现在完成时否定在 have/has 后加 not。

exercises.q: He has gone to the library. (改为一般疑问句)
exercises.answer: Has he gone to the library?
exercises.explain: 现在完成时疑问句将 have/has 提到主语前。

exercises.q: They have visited the Great Wall. (用 she 改写)
exercises.answer: She has visited the Great Wall.
exercises.explain: 主语变为第三人称单数时，have 要改为 has。

exercises.q: I have saw that film before.
exercises.answer: I have seen that film before.
exercises.explain: 现在完成时中 have 后要用过去分词 seen，不是 saw。

exercises.q: She have finished her work.
exercises.explain: 主语是第三人称单数 she，要用 has 而不是 have。

exercises.q: He ______ in this school since he was seven.
exercises.explain: since 引导时间状语从句，主句用现在完成时。

exercises.q: —Where is Tom? —He ______ to the supermarket.
exercises.explain: has gone 表示去了还没回来，符合语境。

exercises.q: I ______ my pen. Can I use yours?
exercises.explain: 丢失钢笔对现在有影响，用现在完成时。

exercises.q: She ______ the book for two weeks.
exercises.explain: borrow 是短暂动词，不能与 for two weeks 连用，要用延续性动词 keep。

exercises.q: We ______ each other since we were children.
exercises.explain: since 引导过去时间，主句用现在完成时表示持续。

exercises.q: The film ______ (be) on for half an hour.
exercises.explain: for half an hour 表示持续一段时间，用现在完成时。

exercises.q: How long ______ you ______ (have) this bike?
exercises.explain: 询问拥有某物多久，用现在完成时，have 的过去分词是 had。

exercises.q: She ______ already ______ (make) a decision.
exercises.explain: already 是现在完成时标志词，主语 she 用 has。

exercises.q: He has joined the club for three years.
exercises.explain: join 是短暂动词，不能与 for three years 连用，应改为 has been in。

exercises.q: I haven't heard from him recently.
exercises.explain: recently 是现在完成时标志词，否定形式正确。

exercises.q: The meeting began ten minutes ago. (改为现在完成时)
exercises.answer: The meeting has been on for ten minutes.
exercises.explain: begin 是短暂动词，改为现在完成时需用延续性表达 has been on。

exercises.q: He came here two days ago. (用 for two days 改写)
exercises.answer: He has been here for two days.
exercises.explain: 短暂动词 come 改为延续性表达 has been here。

exercises.q: I have never read such an interesting book. (改为一般疑问句)
exercises.answer: Have you ever read such an interesting book?
exercises.explain: 改为疑问句时 never 变为 ever，have 提前。

exercises.q: She has bought the car for three years.
exercises.answer: She has had the car for three years.
exercises.explain: buy 是短暂动词，不能与 for 时间段连用，应改为 has had。

exercises.q: I have finished my homework two hours ago.
exercises.answer: I finished my homework two hours ago.
exercises.explain: two hours ago 是具体过去时间，应用一般过去时。

exercises.q: By the time we arrived, the concert ______ already ______.
exercises.explain: by the time 引导过去时间，表示过去的过去，用过去完成时。

exercises.q: It is the first time that I ______ such a beautiful sunset.
exercises.explain: It is the first time that 后用现在完成时。

exercises.q: He ______ in this company since he graduated from college.
exercises.explain: since 引导过去时间点，主句用现在完成时。

exercises.q: The children ______ the classroom. It looks clean now.
exercises.explain: 过去动作对现在有影响，用现在完成时。

exercises.q: I ______ my keys. I can't open the door.
exercises.explain: 丢失钥匙对现在造成影响，用现在完成时。

exercises.q: So far, no one ______ (be) able to solve the problem.
exercises.explain: so far 是现在完成时标志词，no one 用 has。

exercises.q: This is the most interesting book I ______ ever ______ (read).
exercises.explain: 最高级与 ever 连用，用现在完成时。

exercises.q: He ______ (not appear) in public since the incident.
exercises.explain: since 引导过去时间，主句用现在完成时否定。

exercises.q: I have been knowing him for ten years.
exercises.explain: know 是状态动词，不能用于进行时，应改为 have known。

exercises.q: She has gone to Paris three times this year.
exercises.explain: 表示去过多次应用 has been to，has gone to 表示去了还没回来。

exercises.q: He joined the army three years ago. (改为现在完成时)
exercises.answer: He has been in the army for three years.
exercises.explain: join 是短暂动词，改为现在完成时需用 has been in。

exercises.q: I last saw him two weeks ago. (用 since 改写)
exercises.answer: I haven't seen him since two weeks ago.
exercises.explain: last saw 改为 since 结构，用现在完成时否定。

exercises.q: The old man died five years ago. (改为现在完成时)
exercises.answer: The old man has been dead for five years.
exercises.explain: die 是短暂动词，改为现在完成时需用 has been dead。

exercises.q: I have received his letter for a week.
exercises.answer: I have had his letter for a week.
exercises.explain: receive 是短暂动词，不能与 for 时间段连用，应改为 have had。

exercises.q: It has rained yesterday.
exercises.explain: yesterday 是具体过去时间，应用一般过去时。

exercises.q: I ______ my homework, so I can go out to play now.
exercises.explain: 强调过去完成的动作对现在造成的影响（可以出去玩了），用现在完成时。

exercises.q: She ______ in this school since 2020.
exercises.explain: since 引导的时间状语表示动作从过去持续到现在，用现在完成时。

exercises.q: We ______ each other for ten years.
exercises.explain: for ten years 表示持续一段时间，know 用现在完成时表示状态延续。

exercises.q: He ______ to Beijing twice.
exercises.explain: twice 表示经历，用 have/has been to 表示去过某地。

exercises.q: ______ you ever ______ a panda?
exercises.explain: ever 常与现在完成时连用，询问某人是否有过某种经历。

exercises.q: They ______ (already / eat) lunch, so they are not hungry.
exercises.explain: already 常放在 have/has 和过去分词之间，表示已经完成的动作。

exercises.q: My brother ______ (not finish) his project yet.
exercises.explain: yet 用于否定句中表示尚未完成的动作，用现在完成时。

exercises.q: How long ______ you ______ (live) here?
exercises.explain: How long 询问持续的时间长度，用现在完成时。

exercises.q: The sentence "I have seen this movie yesterday." is grammatically correct.
exercises.explain: yesterday 是具体的过去时间，不能与现在完成时连用，应改为一般过去时。

exercises.q: The sentence "She has lost her key, so she can't open the door." is grammatically correct.
exercises.explain: 丢钥匙的动作发生在过去，但对现在有影响（开不了门），用现在完成时正确。

exercises.q: Rewrite the sentence in negative form: I have finished my work.
exercises.answer: I have not finished my work.
exercises.explain: 现在完成时的否定形式是在 have/has 后加 not。

exercises.q: Rewrite the sentence as a question: They have visited the museum.
exercises.explain: 现在完成时的一般疑问句将 have/has 提到主语前。

exercises.q: Rewrite using "just": She has arrived.
exercises.explain: just 表示刚刚发生的动作，放在 have/has 和过去分词之间。

exercises.q: I have never saw such a beautiful sunset.

exercises.q: By the time we arrived at the station, the train ______.

exercises.q: I ______ my keys. I can't find them anywhere.

exercises.q: This is the first time I ______ such a delicious meal.

exercises.q: He ______ in this company since he graduated from college.

exercises.q: It is the best book I ______ ever ______ (read).

exercises.q: The sentence "I have known her since we were in primary school." is grammatically correct.
exercises.explain: since 引导的时间状语从句表示从过去持续到现在，主句用现在完成时正确。

exercises.q: The students have wrote their essays and handed them in.

exercises.explain: write 的过去分词是 written，不是 wrote。

exercises.q: I have been knowing him for many years.
exercises.answer: I have known him for many years.

exercises.q: It is the third time that the government ______ such a policy to address the crisis.
exercises.explain: It is the third time that 句型中，从句用现在完成时。

exercises.q: Since the lockdown was declared, a lot of families ______ through a lot of problems.
exercises.explain: since 引导的时间状语表示从过去持续到现在，主句用现在完成时。

exercises.q: By the end of last month, they ______ over 5,000 masks to the local community.
exercises.explain: by the end of last month 表示到过去某个时间点为止，用过去完成时。

exercises.q: No sooner ______ the announcement been made than the crowd burst into cheers.
exercises.explain: No sooner...than 句型中，主句用过去完成时且部分倒装。

exercises.q: The researchers ______ the data for months before they finally published their findings.
exercises.explain: 强调在过去某个时间点之前一直持续进行的动作，用过去完成进行时。

exercises.q: Hardly ______ the meeting begun when the fire alarm went off.
exercises.explain: Hardly...when 句型中，主句用过去完成时且部分倒装。

exercises.q: By the time the rescue team arrived, the survivors ______ (wait) for over 48 hours.
exercises.explain: 强调在过去某个时间点之前持续进行的动作，用过去完成进行时。

exercises.q: It was the most inspiring speech that I ______ ever ______ (hear).
exercises.explain: It was the most...that 句型中，从句用过去完成时表示到过去某时为止的经历。

exercises.q: The sentence "She has been working on this project since three months." is grammatically correct.
exercises.explain: since 后接时间点，three months 是时间段，应改为 for three months。

exercises.q: The sentence "By the time he turned 30, he had already published two novels." is grammatically correct.
exercises.explain: by the time 引导过去时间，主句用过去完成时表示之前已完成的动作。

exercises.q: Rewrite using inversion: The moment he had finished his speech, the audience applauded.
exercises.answer: No sooner had he finished his speech than the audience applauded.
exercises.explain: No sooner...than 句型要求主句部分倒装，用过去完成时。

exercises.q: Rewrite using "since": She started teaching in 2015 and still teaches now.
exercises.explain: since 加时间点，主句用现在完成进行时表示从过去持续到现在的动作。

exercises.q: Rewrite using "before": They had never experienced such a severe earthquake until last year.
exercises.answer: They had never experienced such a severe earthquake before last year.
exercises.explain: before 加过去时间点，与过去完成时连用表示到那时为止的经历。

exercises.answer: Having finished his homework, he decided to take a break.
exercises.explain: 现在分词的完成式主动形式是 having done，不需要 been。

exercises.q: The committee has been discussing the proposal since the last meeting was held, but they have not reached a consensus yet.
exercises.answer: The committee has been discussing the proposal since the last meeting was held, but they have not reached a consensus yet.
exercises.explain: 该句语法正确，since 引导时间状语，主句用现在完成进行时，yet 用于否定句。

grammar.key: Modal Verb: 'ought to' / 情态动词 'ought to'
grammar.title: 情态动词 ought to：义务、建议与 should / must / had better 的辨析
grammar.titleEn: Modal Verb 'ought to': Obligation, Advice and Contrast with should / must / had better
grammar.usage:
ought to 是情态动词，核心结构为“主语 + ought to + 动词原形”，用来表达道义上的责任、义务、强烈的建议或按常理应当发生的事。它不随主语人称和数的变化而变化，后面永远接动词原形，不能接不定式的 to，也不能接动名词或过去式。

肯定句：主语 + ought to + 动词原形。例如：You ought to tell the truth. 否定句：主语 + ought not to + 动词原形，缩写为 oughtn't to。例如：You oughtn't to stay up so late. 疑问句：Ought + 主语 + to + 动词原形？例如：Ought we to inform the teacher? 不过在现代英语中，ought to 的疑问句比较正式，日常口语更常用 should。

ought to 与 should 意思非常接近，都表示“应该”，但 ought to 更强调客观上的责任、道义或按规则理应如此，语气略正式；should 则更偏主观看法和个人建议。ought to 与 must 的区别在于：must 表示“必须”，语气最强，常指说话人施加的义务或强制要求；ought to 表示“理应、应当”，语气弱于 must，暗示如果不做，虽然不好，但不一定造成严重后果。ought to 与 had better 的区别在于：had better 表示“最好做某事”，带有警告或威胁意味，常指如果不做会有不良后果；ought to 更偏向道德或责任层面的建议。

初中阶段主要要求掌握 ought to 的基本结构，能把它替换成 should 来理解句意；高中阶段则要求能在书面表达中恰当使用 ought to 体现正式、客观的语气，并能区分 ought to / should / must / had better 在语域和语义强度上的差异。高考书面表达中，适当使用 ought to 可以提升语言的正式感和多样性，但不宜与 should 随意混用造成语气不一致。

易错点一：ought to 后面必须接动词原形，不能写成 ought to doing 或 ought to to do。易错点二：否定形式是 ought not to，而不是 don't ought to 或 oughtn't。易错点三：疑问句要把 ought 提到主语前，而不是用 do/does 来构成。易错点四：ought to 没有过去式，表示过去的义务时常用 ought to have done，意为“本应该做而未做”。
forms: 肯定式：主语 + ought to + 动词原形
否定式：主语 + ought not to / oughtn't to + 动词原形
疑问式：Ought + 主语 + to + 动词原形？
过去义务：主语 + ought to have + 过去分词（本应该做而未做）
否定过去义务：主语 + ought not to have + 过去分词（本不该做却做了）
notes: ought to 后只能接动词原形，不能接 doing、to do 或过去式。
否定形式是 ought not to，不要写成 don't ought to 或 oughtn't。
ought to 的疑问句较正式，高考书面语中可用，但口语中更常见 should。
ought to have done 表示“过去本应做而未做”，是高考语法填空和写作中的高频结构。
ought to 比 should 更正式、更客观，适合用于议论文、建议信等书面语体；日常口语中 should 更自然。

examples.cn: 你不应该玩太长时间电脑游戏。

examples.cn: 学生应该按时交作业。

exercises.q: You ______ do your homework before you watch TV.
exercises.explain: ought to 后接动词原形，表示应该做某事。

exercises.q: We ______ be kind to our classmates.
exercises.explain: ought to 表示道义上的责任，后接动词原形 be。

exercises.q: She ______ eat too much candy. It's bad for her teeth.
exercises.explain: ought to 的否定形式是 ought not to，表示不应该。

exercises.q: You look tired. You ______ go to bed early tonight.
exercises.explain: ought to 用于提出强烈建议，后接动词原形。

exercises.q: Students ______ listen to the teacher in class.
exercises.explain: ought to 表示学生应尽的义务。

exercises.q: We ______ to help our parents at home.
exercises.explain: ought to 是固定搭配，表示应该帮助父母。

exercises.q: You ______ not to run in the hallway.
exercises.explain: ought not to 表示不应该在走廊里跑。

exercises.q: He ______ to say sorry to his friend.
exercises.explain: ought to 表示道义上应该道歉。

exercises.q: The sentence "She ought to helps her mother." is correct.
exercises.explain: ought to 后必须接动词原形，不能接 helps。

exercises.q: The sentence "We ought not to be late for school." is correct.
exercises.explain: ought not to 后接动词原形 be，结构正确。
